Which U.S. states had an increase in registered gasoline cars from 2021 to 2022 according to the Department of Energy, a percentage decrease in traffic fatalities from 2021 to 2022 according to state traffic data from NHTSA, and had under approximately 90 million metric tons of total CO2 emissions in 2023 according to the EIA?

2. Percentage decrease in traffic fatalities from 2021 to 2022 per state, using NHTSA state traffic data.

We need dataset: DOE (Department of Energy) vehicle registration counts by state per fuel type. The DOJ? # Vehicle Registration Counts by State

Year 
This page provides approximate light-duty vehicle registration counts derived by the National Laboratory of the Rockies with data from Experian Information Solutions. Counts are rounded to the closest 100 vehicles and reflect the total number of light-duty registered vehicles through the selected year. Fuel types are based on vehicle identification numbers (VINs), which do not reflect aftermarket conversions to use different fuels or power sources.

For a map comparing the density of light-duty vehicles per state and charts comparing registration counts over time, see [TransAtlas](https://afdc.energy.gov/transatlas/).

Year 
This page provides approximate light-duty vehicle registration counts derived by the National Laboratory of the Rockies with data from Experian Information Solutions. Fuel types are based on vehicle identification numbers (VINs), which do not reflect aftermarket conversions to use different fuels or power sources.

### About

The term _energy-related CO 2 emissions_ refers to emissions from primary energy consumption of fossil fuels (coal, natural gas, and petroleum) at the location where the fuels are consumed in the residential, commercial, industrial, transportation, and electric power sectors.   
**Read the full report** ([SEDS State Energy CO2 Emissions Estimates](https://www.eia.gov/state/seds/sep_co2/notes/co2_print.pdf "SEDS documentation"))

  

**State emissions methodology**  
See the [State Energy Data System (SEDS) Technical notes & documentation](https://www.eia.gov/state/seds/seds-technical-notes-complete.php?sid=US "State emissions methodology") for the methods and data sources used to estimate state CO 2 emissions.

#### Other EIA state-related links

[State Energy Data System (SEDS)](https://www.eia.gov/state/seds/) is EIA's main repository for state-level energy data and the estimates the underlying energy consumption data used to calculate state CO 2 emissions.

[State Energy Portal](https://www.eia.gov/beta/states/overview) offers multiple ways to examine energy and energy-related CO 2 emissions data and contains narratives and rankings for each state.

[Electric power industry data from survey forms EIA-860 and EIA-923](https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/detail-data.php) include sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxide, and CO 2 emissions from generating electricity in the electric power, industrial, and commercial sectors since 1990.

[State Electricity Profiles](https://www.eia.gov/electricity/state/) provides data for net interstate flow of electricity, as well as state electric power capacity, generation, emissions, and more.

### About

The term _energy-related CO 2 emissions_ refers to emissions from primary energy consumption of fossil fuels (coal, natural gas, and petroleum) at the location where the fuels are consumed in the residential, commercial, industrial, transportation, and electric power sectors.   
**Read the full report** ([SEDS State Energy CO2 Emissions Estimates](https://www.eia.gov/state/seds/sep_co2/notes/co2_print.pdf "SEDS documentation"))
